title: Ukraine strikes Putin prized Crimean Bridge , destroys central road section ahead of US - China meet
full_text: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea on Tuesday, destroying its central road section and sending part of the structure crashing into the sea. The attack, carried out using drones and missiles, has disrupted a key supply route for Russian forces and comes two days before President Vladimir Putin is due to meet the leaders of China and the US.Footage show that the bridge's main road arch had collapsed into the sea, leaving a large gap in the structure. Russian officials said road traffic had been suspended, while rail services had partly resumed.The damage has disrupted a direct supply route to Crimea, increasing Russia's reliance on routes through occupied mainland Ukraine.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the attack as an "unprecedented operation" that had been weeks in the making. He said it was carried out by the Ukraine Security Service along with all of Ukraine's forces."Russia strikes our infrastructure every day, including bridges," Zelenskyy said. "We are ... reminding Russia that war will always return to where it began."In his video address, Zelenskyy said Ukraine had repeatedly urged Moscow to stop attacking infrastructure but Russia had continued to escalate the conflict."We have long been telling Russia: Enough of striking bridges, cities and villages, energy infrastructure, railways and grain ships. Enough of war," Zelenskyy said, as cited by Reuters. "But ​every time Russia chooses further escalation."Meanwhile, Kremlin said that it would rebuild the bridge "better than before".Why the Crimean Bridge matters to RussiaThe 19-km (12-mile) bridge is a major road and rail connection between Russia and occupied Crimea. It also serves as a route for Russian soldiers travelling towards the front line, making it an important link for Moscow's military operations.Ukraine has targeted the bridge several times but has struggled to shut it down permanently. The latest attack has damaged a key section and disrupted road traffic, while rail services have only partly resumed.Kyiv has also been targeting Russian oil refineries and depots to increase the economic cost of the war. Striking the bridge is another attempt to put pressure on Putin, this time by raising the political cost of the conflict.Putin's personal projectThe bridge, built in 2014, has particular significance for Putin. It is widely seen in both Russia and Ukraine as the Russian president's personal project and a symbol of Moscow's control over the peninsula.The $3.6 billion (£2.7 billion) infrastructure project was built by Arkady Rotenberg, a tycoon and close friend of Putin. The Russian president personally inaugurated it in May 2018 by driving a lorry across it.The timing of the attack is also significant, coming just two days before Putin is due to meet the leaders of China and the US. The damage could overshadow his return to the international spotlight.Meanwhile, in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic had partially resumed on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges, key crossings over the Dnipro River.
